items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Who criticized the subject centered traditional curriculum?
items.x:
Printed key: Alfred North Whitehead. Many pedagogy books instead link John Dewey with the criticism of the subject-centred traditional curriculum (child-centred / activity curriculum).
A.N. Whitehead ('The Aims of Education') attacked 'inert ideas' and the fatal disconnection of subjects in the traditional curriculum; the printed key is Whitehead.

items.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
items.s: In which season Vitamin A is required in higher quantities?
items.x: No standard source (ICMR-NIN RDA) gives a season-specific vitamin A requirement; deficiency signs such as night blindness peak in the hot pre-harvest season, while the printed key says winter. Left unkeyed. Off-topic (nutrition).

items.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: If a person closes one eye and looks with the other eye only, he would see?
items.x: With one eye we lose binocular depth perception, so the world looks flat, i.e. two-dimensional (the usual key). Colour vision is not lost.

items.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
items.s: Which of the elements found in human body has functional requirement?
items.x:
Official key: Arsenic. Strictly: arsenic's essentiality in humans is unproven (it is a toxic element); none of the options is an established essential element.
Among the options only arsenic is treated as a (possibly essential) ultra-trace element with a functional role; titanium, caesium and aluminium have no known requirement.

items.s: Holography is a technique which is now extensively used by:
items.x:
Printed/book key: Navigators. Strictly: holography is used widely by museum authorities (3D recording/display of artefacts) and in security; no source found stating 'navigators' (web search).
Printed key: navigators (holographic displays/head-up navigation aids). Holograms are also widely used to record and display museum artefacts, so the option is debatable.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
items.s:
A statement is given followed by two conclusions.
Select the correct response from the given options.
Statement: Aschelminthes are called roundworms.
Conclusion:
i. The body of the aschelminthes is circular in cross-section.
ii. Roundworms have organ-system level of body organisation.
items.x:
Printed key: only (i) follows from the statement. Strictly, both (i) and (ii) are true facts (PMF General Science p.89 / NCERT XI: organ-system level), so a fact-check reading gives 'both'.
The name 'roundworm' comes from the body being circular in cross-section, so conclusion (i) follows from the statement. Conclusion (ii) is a true fact (Aschelminthes have organ-system level of organisation) but does not follow from the statement about the name.

items.s: Which among the following institutions hosted the 106th Indian Science Congress in 2018?
items.x:
Printed key: Central University of Manipur (the 2018 session, 105th). Strictly the 106th session was at Lovely Professional University, Jalandhar, in January 2019 (Wikipedia ISCA sessions table).
The 2018 session (the 105th, March 2018) was hosted by Manipur University, Imphal, the key here; the 106th was at Lovely Professional University, Jalandhar, in January 2019.

items.s: Choose the incorrect short-cut key combinations of Tally ERP9 in the given below:
items.x: Unscorable: in Tally ERP 9 all four are valid - Alt+2 duplicates a voucher, Alt+A adds, Alt+I inserts, and Alt+D deletes a voucher, master or (in Company Alteration) a company - so no combination is incorrect.

items.s: The largest Telecom operator in India is
items.x:
BSNL was the largest operator in 2003 — now Reliance Jio is the largest by subscribers (general knowledge, TRAI data)
In 2003 BSNL was India's largest telecom operator.

items.s:
Consider the following:

a. Satellites move around the earth with the same speed as the Earth spins

b. Satellites cover every part of earth except poles and surrounding areas which are out of their range
o: Both a and b are true
Neither a nor b is true
items.x:
No printed key. If the stem means geostationary satellites only, both a and b would be true (option c).
Taken generally, neither holds: only geostationary satellites keep pace with the Earth's spin, and polar-orbiting satellites do cover the poles.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-II Ward Planning and Regula
items.s: Which among the following is not an Indian Remote Sensing Satellite System?
items.x:
Printed key: AstroSat. Strictly: NavIC (navigation) is not an IRS satellite either, so two options fit.
AstroSat is a space observatory, not an IRS (remote sensing) satellite; ResourceSat and OceanSat are IRS satellites.

items.s:
Match the nomenclature used for space travellers in different countries/continent

A. Russia
B. USA
C. China
D. Germany
i. Astronaut ii. Taikonaut iii. Spationaut iv. Cosmonaut
items.x:
Official key: Germany – Spationaut. Strictly: 'spationaut' is the French term; Germany uses astronaut.
Russia uses cosmonaut, the USA astronaut and China taikonaut; spationaut (France) is left for Germany, so option 2 is the only possible match.

items.s: The State which has highest Atomic Reactors in the country is
items.x:
Printed key: Tamil Nadu. Strictly: Rajasthan (Rawatbhata) has the most power reactors; among the options Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu each had about four in 2016 (general knowledge, not checked).
The printed key is Tamil Nadu: in 2016 it had Kudankulam and Madras (Kalpakkam) reactors, plus the Kalpakkam research and fast-breeder reactors. Strictly, Rajasthan (RAPS, Rawatbhata) has the most power reactors, but it is not offered.

items.s: According to reports of Central Pollution Control Board of India, what was the average air quality index (AQI) of Delhi in 2021?
items.x: Printed key: 144. Caution: CAQM/CPCB-based reports give Delhi's 2021 daily-average AQI as about 209 for the whole year, so the 144 figure may refer to a part of the year or a different metric. (AQI item, moved.)
